minutes.headline: Select Board reappointed a Monty Tech representative, appointed a sewer commissioner, approved a liquor license transfer, and began ranking ARPA requests.
minutes.summary: The board handled appointments (Monty Tech representative, veterans services agent, sewer commissioner in a joint meeting, lifeguard) and held a hearing approving transfer of a wine and malt license for Baker's Variety. It then set a process for ranking ARPA requests ahead of August 1 and began brainstorming FY24 board goals. The town manager reported on vacancies, facilities and a senior tax exemption bill.

public_comment.topic: Clarified that the Sewer Commission made no new funding request; its ask remained manholes and pump stations.
Mr. McDonald (on Zoom) thanked Mike Mackin and urged volunteerism for town boards.
Supported the transfer to the new owner and thanked the town after 35 years.
Supported the license transfer and noted the buyer's interest in a home in Lunenburg.

votes.motion: Appoint Barbara Reynolds as Montachusett Regional School representative (term first stated to 2027, amended to June 30 2028)
Ratify town manager's appointment of Michelle durkey as veterans services agent
Approve transfer of wine and malt license to Mahant Baker's Variety Inc, including common victualler, three automatic amusement devices and video game licenses
Jointly appoint Mike Mackin to the Sewer Commission (roll call)
Ratify town manager's appointment of Cole Kiefer as seasonal lifeguard
Authorize chair to sign letter to ABCC withdrawing the Jax Country Variety transfer to Pure Inc

budget_items.what_was_said: Sewer chair said the request was unchanged, for manholes and pump stations, and that the 305 figure was a rounded pump station cost.
Payroll, payroll deduction and accounts payable warrants were reported; payroll was low because schools are not in session.
Ambulance and two DPW trucks were committed but may be reconsidered, possibly funded from special purpose stabilization instead, freeing ARPA money.
figures_as_heard: nine hundred and eighty six thousand dollars

budget_items.what_was_said: Parks Commissioners received a commitment but hoped for more.
Town manager said the software is very expensive to adopt; go-live set for September.
A member referred to the town losing revenue, making a 30 School Street project poorly timed.

decisions.decision: Members to submit ARPA rankings to the chair by Friday the 28th; the August 1 meeting will focus on ARPA.
Public schools plow truck request removed from the ARPA list; flat Hill drainage and PFAS items kept as placeholders.
Committed ambulance and DPW truck funds excluded from the ranking exercise for now.
FY24 goals: continue the bylaws review and add a buildings goal combining municipal building design and 30 School Street, to be worded later.
Update on the investigation report targeted for the August 15 meeting.

what_happened.line: The board set a process for ranking ARPA requests: rankings due to the chair by the 28th, and the August 1 meeting to focus on ARPA.
The board removed the public schools plow truck request from the ARPA list and kept the flat Hill drainage and PFAS items as placeholders.
The committed ambulance and DPW truck funds were left out of the ranking for now, though they may be reconsidered or paid from another source.
The board unanimously approved transferring the wine and malt license, with related licenses, to Mahant Baker's Variety Inc after a public hearing.
The board reappointed a Monty Tech representative and, in a joint meeting with the Sewer Commission, unanimously appointed Mike Mackin to that commission.

why_it_matters: ARPA money is limited and one-time, so the ranking set here decides which town projects, such as sewer, drainage and PFAS work, get funded and which wait.
If the committed ambulance and DPW trucks are paid from special purpose stabilization instead, more ARPA money would be available for other requests, though the board has not decided that.
